title: Quantization run archival shipyard and approval flow
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Implement a 'shipyard' for quantization calibration runs that standardizes: artifact escrow, TTL-based archival, staged approval gates, tenant-scoped ACLs, and an approval audit trail visible in Redwood Console. This work covers product flows, acceptance criteria for accuracy gating, and the run lifecycle UI/permissions required to safely promote, restore, or prune FP8/INT8 calibration artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a Run detail page with explicit 'Archive', 'Promote', and 'Quarantine' actions that respect project-level RBAC
Admins can configure three TTL tiers (ephemeral 7d, working 30d, archived 365d) and apply per-project defaults
Archived calibration artifacts are immutable and have signed provenance metadata visible in UI
Automated accuracy-validation step flags runs that regress against golden prompt sets and prevents promotion until approved
Audit trail entries are generated for every lifecycle transition (create, mark-archived, restore, promote, delete) and stored for 1 year
APIs and console honor cross-tenant isolation: no artifact leak across tenants by default
End-to-end e2e tests and a staging PR are merged with runtime integration tests against sample FP8/INT8 artifacts

decisions: Use three TTL tiers (7/30/365 days) as configurable defaults per project rather than per-run to reduce UI complexity
Archive artifacts will be immutable; promotion creates a new signed snapshot to guarantee reproducibility
Accuracy regression blocks auto-promotion; manual override requires Admin role and creates an audit entry
Implement audit retention as 1 year by default with an admin-configurable max of 3 years pending legal review
blockers: ENG-21402: signature and provenance library needs production hardening for high-throughput calibration runs
Legal sign-off on maximum audit retention window (waiting for counsel response)
Dependence on Console RBAC feature parity for 'project operator' role
